cejstSummary: Using the local Justice40 / CEJST tract snapshot, 11 of 14 census tracts in Gibson County are flagged as disadvantaged (78.6%). 0 tracts carry the water and wastewater stress flag, and 11 tracts carry the climate stress flag.

overview: Gibson County is represented as a West Tennessee county summary focused on county-scale watershed conditions, public-interest infrastructure context, and environmental screening indicators. It intersects North Fork Forked Deer, South Fork Obion, Obion and overlaps 3 state legislative district labels plus 1 congressional district labels.

indicators.label: Poverty rate
indicators.definition: Share of people below the poverty level based on ACS table B17001.
indicators.caveat: County-wide rates can hide tract-level variation.

stateRank.basis: Ranked by ACS county poverty rate, high to low.

indicators.label: Disadvantaged tracts
indicators.definition: Share of county tracts flagged as disadvantaged in the local Justice40 / CEJST tract snapshot.
indicators.caveat: Justice40 is a screening context, not a final judgment about community need.

stateRank.basis: Ranked by share of county tracts flagged as disadvantaged, high to low.

indicators.label: Impaired river miles
indicators.definition: Approximate river miles intersecting county boundaries in 2026 not supporting impairment categories.
indicators.caveat: Line segments are spatially intersected with county boundaries, so shared waters can contribute to multiple counties.

stateRank.basis: Ranked by impaired river miles, high to low.

indicators.label: Monitoring stations
indicators.definition: Distinct DWR water-quality monitoring stations associated with the county.
indicators.caveat: Station presence does not by itself indicate adequate monitoring coverage or condition.

indicators.label: Active water permits
indicators.definition: Count of active permitted features associated with the county in the local permit layer.
